- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day average), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.30 for 3+ consecutive days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or neutral (e.g., sentiment < -0.20 for 5+ days); adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price tends to rise 1–3 days after model peak; shift forecast peak 1–2 days earlier to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative after a bullish run, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the first 5 days post-sentiment shift.
